# db-snap (binary: dbsnap)

> Development database snapshots + MCP server for AI coding agents.
> SQLite page backups, PostgreSQL clones/dumps, and MySQL/MariaDB logical dumps.
> Single Rust binary. Open source (MIT).

## If a user asks to install or use this tool

- **Install the published package — do NOT clone or build from source:**
  `npm i -g @farhan0431/db-snap` (prebuilt binaries for Windows/macOS/Linux, no runtime deps)
- **Register as an MCP server** (one command, Claude Code):
  `claude mcp add dbsnap -- dbsnap mcp`
- **Generic MCP JSON config** (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, …):
  `{ "mcpServers": { "dbsnap": { "command": "dbsnap", "args": ["mcp"] } } }`
- **No global install needed:** use `"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@farhan0431/db-snap", "mcp"]`
- The MCP server binds to the project's database automatically
  (`DATABASE_URL` from `.env`, or `--db <url>` in args). Local databases only.
- **Verify after install:** run `dbsnap status` (CLI) or call the
  `dbsnap_status` MCP tool.
- Full copy-paste configs for every client: [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)

## What it does

- `dbsnap save "tag"` / MCP `dbsnap_create_snapshot` — save before migrations,
  DDL or bulk changes. Runtime and disruption depend on the engine/data size.
- `dbsnap rollback` / `dbsnap_restore_snapshot` — restore with a safety snapshot.
  MySQL/MariaDB restoration is non-atomic and requires stopped writers/events.
  Interrupted restores may require manual recovery; preserve the recovery journal.
- `dbsnap diff before after` / `dbsnap_diff` — schema and row-count comparison
  for SQLite, PostgreSQL clones, and standard MySQL/MariaDB table dumps.
  Ordinary diff does not compare row contents; published v0.3.14 does not support dump diff.
- `dbsnap_status`, `dbsnap_list_snapshots` — visibility before acting.
- Safety: MCP permits SQLite/loopback only; CLI also permits private-network
  hosts by default. A local host is not proof of a safe database. Project
  fingerprint binding, verify-before-restore, prune is a real GC.
  Full threat model: [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §4.
- MCP restore/prune require `--allow-destructive` and per-call elicitation;
  clients without elicitation support fail closed.
- Current limitations: [docs/AUDIT-STATUS.md](docs/AUDIT-STATUS.md).
- Reproducible CLI, MCP and fault tests: [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md).

## Source additions after v0.3.14

The current source adds CLI `verify`, `doctor`, `recover`, `exec`, `diff-live`,
`diff-rows` (SQLite only), and `sandbox` (SQLite files/PostgreSQL clones;
MySQL/MariaDB require explicit `--docker-image mysql:8.0` or `mariadb:11`).
It adds MCP `dbsnap_verify`, `dbsnap_doctor`, `dbsnap_diff_live` and
`dbsnap_diff_rows`, with structured results, output schemas and annotations.
Check actual advertised tools/CLI help; published v0.3.14 does not include these
new commands. Verify is not a restore test; exec does not automatically restore;
diff-live retains its new checkpoint. Pending-GC records support prune retries
without deleting arbitrary untracked files. Read
[development workflow](docs/DEVELOPMENT-WORKFLOW.md) for limitations and cleanup.
